questions.q: Explain why solving a differential equation gives a family of functions rather than a single number.
questions.answer: A differential equation only constrains the derivative, not the exact function; any constant added to a valid solution $y$ has derivative $0$ and doesn't change whether it solves the equation, so every $y=$ (that solution) $+C$ also works — a whole family, not one answer.
